title: add-jsonschema-response-format-strict-mode-and-improved-errors-openai-compat
author: Avery Chen
description: This PR adds first-class JSON Schema support to the response_format API surface, introduces a strict validation mode with clearer error reporting, and updates the OpenAI-compatibility layer to expose the new behavior. Motivation: customers expect predictable structured outputs (for evals, tool calls, and downstream parsing). Prior implementations returned ad-hoc validation errors and inconsistent behavior between the Redwood API and our OpenAI compatibility shim. This change standardizes schema handling and error messages and makes strict mode opt-in. Changes include: - new response_format="json_schema" option on generation/chat endpoints - response_format.schema (JSON Schema draft-07 compatible) accepted as a string or JSON object (OpenAI compat accepts object) - strict_mode boolean: when true, model output is validated against the schema and model failure returns a 400 with structured error details; when false, we attempt best-effort repair and include validation warnings in the response extras - improved validation error payload (path, expected, actual, suggestion) - server-side validation + optional client-side (SDK) preflight check route - OpenAI compatibility layer: map new error payloads to legacy-style error codes and add a compatibility header when strict semantics are enabled - docs + SDK updates and migration notes (see release_notes). Checklist: - [x] Implement server-side schema parsing & validation - [x] Add strict mode enforcement and improved error structure - [x] Update OpenAI compatibility adapter and headers - [x] Add unit + integration tests covering typical and edge cases - [x] Update Python/TS SDK typing & docs - [x] Add migration notes and changelog entries Linear: ENG-1548, PM-3221. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged (strict_mode=false) and legacy clients continue to receive best-effort responses. Breaking changes: none by default; enabling strict_mode is a behavioral change that may cause validation errors to be surfaced. See release_notes for migration guidance.

f7e3a11: tests + fixtures for schema edge cases

discussion:
Samir: Can we confirm which JSON Schema draft we support?
Avery: We're standardizing on draft-07 for compatibility with our existing validators; noted in docs.
Jillian: For strict_mode failures, can we include a suggested repair string to help users?
Avery: Added a "suggestion" field in the error payload with a minimal example and a pointer to docs.
Diego: Will the OpenAI shim translate the new error structure to an appropriate code?
Avery: Yes — adapter maps to openai.error codes and adds X-Redwood-Strict-Compat header when strict semantics are in effect.
Samir: Add integration tests for multi-turn generation with schema and KV cache interactions.
Avery: Added tests in test/integration/jsonschema_strict_mode_test.go. CI initially failed on lint; fixed import ordering and re-ran. All checks passed before merge.
release_notes:
- Added response_format="json_schema" with optional schema and strict_mode flag
- Strict mode enforces schema validation and returns structured errors (path, expected, actual, suggestion)
- OpenAI-compat adapter maps errors and exposes compatibility headers
- SDKs and docs updated with examples and migration guidance
